It is very quiet in the library.

他比我矮一点儿。: 这里很安全，你可以放心。
It is safe here, so you can relax.
The room is very clean.
These trousers are too short.
This book is too old.
column6: 旧 is for things that are no longer new. For a person, use 老.

My grandfather is already very old.
column6: 老 is also a friendly prefix before a surname or title, as in 老师.

This watermelon is very sweet.
The sky is very blue.
She likes yellow skirts.
This fruit is very fresh.
This question is very simple.
This character is hard to write.
This piece of clothing is too ugly.
He sings badly.
This is a difficult problem.
This question is not easy.
It is convenient to take the subway here.
This piece of clothing fits well.

他比我矮一点儿。: 请你再说一遍，我没听清楚。
Please say it again. I did not hear it clearly.
How strange. Why hasn't he come yet?
This meeting is very important.

他比我矮一点儿。: 这里的主要问题是什么？
What is the main problem here?
Don't rush. Speak slowly.
This restaurant is very famous.
This book is very useful.
These two characters have different meanings.
My phone is the same as yours.
I usually get up at seven.

他比我矮一点儿。: 这个房间的环境有点儿差。
The environment of this room is a bit poor.
We two are about the same height.

他比我矮一点儿。: 这是一个很常见的名字。
This is a very common name.
This is a commonly used Chinese character.
The size of these shoes is wrong.
There are a lot of people in the park.

short (in height); low: for a long time; a long time
We have not met for a long time.
Have you been waiting long?
He has not been in China long.
There are four seasons in a year.
column6: 季 is mostly used inside words: 四季, 季节.

There is nobody in the classroom.
column6: 室 means a room and is used in words like 教室 and 办公室.

The flowers in the garden have all bloomed.
column6: 园 is mostly used inside words: 公园, 花园, 动物园, 校园.

short (in height); low: person engaged in a job or a group
My older brother is an athlete.
column6: 员 comes at the end of a word for a person in a job or group: 运动员.

There are two cups on the table.
column6: 子 is a light suffix on many nouns: 桌子, 杯子, 房子, 筷子. It is read zi, with no tone.

他比我矮一点儿。: 在这件事中，他帮了我很多。
In this matter, he helped me a lot.
column6: 中 here goes after a noun and means "in": 事中, 书中, 生活中.

Her voice is very pleasant.
Is your name on the list?
Your level of Chinese is very high.
I have a good way to do it.
What is a good way to learn Chinese?

他比我矮一点儿。: 我想有机会去中国学习。
I hope to have the chance to study in China.
Their relationship is very good.
column6: 没关系 (it doesn't matter) uses the same word.

他比我矮一点儿。: 你在中国的生活怎么样？
How is your life in China?
column6: 生活 can also be a verb: 他在这里生活了三年.

My umbrella was taken away by a friend.
column6: 被 + doer + verb: 我的伞被朋友拿走了. The doer can be left out.

short (in height); low: takes the object before the verb; measure word for things with a handle
Please open the door.
column6: 把 + object + verb + result. 把 is also a measure word for things with a handle: 一把伞.

It is rather cold today.

他比我矮一点儿。: 我喜欢运动，比如游泳、打篮球。
I like sports, for example swimming and playing basketball.
You must arrive before eight.
Do you want anything else?
The other classmates have all gone home.

他比我矮一点儿。: 他不但会说汉语，而且会写汉字。
He can not only speak Chinese but also write characters.

他比我矮一点儿。: 这个菜很好吃，而且很便宜。
This dish is delicious, and it is cheap too.

他比我矮一点儿。: 星期六或星期天，你有时间吗？
Do you have time on Saturday or Sunday?
Either tea or coffee is fine.
column6: 或者 is used in statements. In questions about a choice use 还是.

I want to go, but I do not have time.
Eat first, then go and see a movie.

他比我矮一点儿。: 如果明天下雨，我们就不去了。
If it rains tomorrow, we won't go.

他比我矮一点儿。: 明天下雨的话，我们就不去了。
If it rains tomorrow, we won't go.
column6: 的话 comes after the condition. 如果…的话 is also common.

他比我矮一点儿。: 只要你努力，就一定能学好。
As long as you work hard, you will certainly learn it well.
column6: The pattern is 只要…就…

他比我矮一点儿。: 只有多练习，才能说好汉语。
Only by practising more can you speak Chinese well.
column6: The pattern is 只有…才…

short (in height); low: can only; have no choice but to
他比我矮一点儿。: 现在没有车，我们只能走路。
There are no cars now, so we can only walk.
I am only asking.

他比我矮一点儿。: 除了星期天，我每天都上班。
Except for Sunday, I go to work every day.
column6: 除了…以外 means "except" or "besides". Add 都 for "except", 还/也 for "besides".

I am happy for you.

short (in height); low: in order to; for the purpose of
他比我矮一点儿。: 为了学好汉语，他每天都练习。
In order to learn Chinese well, he practises every day.

他比我矮一点儿。: 我想看一本关于中国的书。
I want to read a book about China.
According to the map, the bank is ahead.

short (in height); low: what to do; what should be done
The phone is lost. What is to be done?
What do you think of this?
Of course you can!
Actually, this character is not hard to write.
He probably gets home at about six.
He seems to be ill.
He comes here almost every day.
This idea is extremely good.
column6: 极 comes after the adjective with 了: 好极了, 累极了.

It is especially cold today.
This movie is quite good.
Today is even colder than yesterday.
The rain is getting heavier and heavier.
column6: The pattern is 越…越…: the more … the more …

short (in height); low: only then; not until; as late as
I did not go to bed until twelve yesterday.
column6: 才 shows something is later, slower or fewer than expected. 就 shows the opposite.

He has just got home.
The meeting has only just ended.
Where did you go just now?
You go first. I will come right away.
I will be there right away.
I will certainly come tomorrow.
How much is it altogether?
Let us go together.

short (in height); low: at the same time; on one side
他比我矮一点儿。: 他一边吃饭，一边看电视。
He watches TV while he eats.
column6: The pattern is 一边…一边… for two actions at the same time.

I have been waiting for you here all along.
He has come again.
column6: 又 is for something that has already happened again. 再 is for something that will happen again.

他比我矮一点儿。: 我终于找到了我的手机。
I have finally found my phone.
He always says he has no time.
She is always the first to arrive in the classroom.
You had better take an umbrella.
Whatever you do, don't forget your passport!
column6: 可 adds strength to a warning, an order or an exclamation: 可别…, 可好了….

We often meet here.
He is often late.
I usually get up at seven.
He suddenly laughed.

short (in height); low: to be delayed; to be late (of a train or plane)
The train is delayed.
Only later did I learn of this.
The day after tomorrow is Friday.
We are going to travel in China the year after next.
We met the day before yesterday.
I went to China the year before last.
Are you busy lately?
What is the last question?
After class, I will go to the library.
I used to live here.

他比我矮一点儿。: 十八岁以上的人可以进去。
People aged 18 and above can go in.

他比我矮一点儿。: 十岁以下的孩子不用买票。
Children under ten do not need to buy a ticket.

他比我矮一点儿。: 学校以外有一家小商店。
There is a small shop outside the school.
He is looking for his phone everywhere.

short (in height); low: need not; there is no need to
You do not need to come. I will go myself.

short (in height); low: to understand; to be clear about
I understand what you mean.
